items.title: Landmark trials at a glance
items.body:
| **Study and link** | **What it contributes to specialist reasoning** |
|---|---|
| [Rivers et al — early goal-directed therapy (2001)](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa010307) | Early protocolised intervention initially appeared beneficial; supplies historical rationale for CVP/ScvO₂ targets, subsequently reassessed in large trials |
| [ProCESS (2014)](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1401602) | Rigorous protocolised EGDT did not outperform contemporary usual care in early septic shock |
| [ARISE (2014)](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1404380) | Australasian multicentre trial reinforced that mandatory invasive EGDT protocol is not superior to modern usual care |
| [ProMISe (2015)](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1500896) | UK trial confirmed no outcome benefit from rigid ScvO₂/CVP-driven EGDT compared with high-quality usual care |
| [ANDROMEDA-SHOCK (2019)](https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2019.0071) | Capillary refill versus lactate-targeted resuscitation; primary mortality comparison not conventionally statistically significant, useful hypothesis-generating physiology |
| [ANDROMEDA-SHOCK-2 (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2025.20402) | Personalised CRT/echo/fluid-responsiveness algorithm improved a hierarchical composite, mainly shorter organ-support duration; not proof of mortality reduction in isolation |
| [CLASSIC (2022)](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2202707) | Post-initial ICU fluid restriction did not reduce 90-day mortality versus standard care |
| [CLOVERS (2023)](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2212663) | Early fluid-restrictive/pressor-forward strategy showed no significant 90-day survival advantage over liberal fluids |
| [ARISE FLUIDS (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2516225) | Australia/NZ-led: early pressor/restricted fluid did not increase days alive and out of hospital at 90 days, though pulmonary oedema was less frequent; supports individualisation |
| [ADRENAL (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1705835) | Hydrocortisone 200 mg/day accelerated shock resolution without statistically significant overall 90-day mortality benefit |
| [APROCCHSS (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1705716) | Hydrocortisone plus fludrocortisone reduced 90-day mortality in a different septic shock population; discuss contrasting inclusion/severity/regimens |
| [BLING III (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2024.9779) | Continuous β-lactam infusion improved clinical cure; primary unadjusted mortality difference not statistically significant, supporting careful evidence interpretation |
| [MERINO (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2018.12163) | Piperacillin–tazobactam not supported as definitive therapy for ceftriaxone-resistant E. coli/Klebsiella bacteraemia relative to meropenem |
| [STOP-IT (2015)](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1411162) | After adequate source control, fixed ≈4-day therapy comparable to longer symptom-driven courses in complicated intra-abdominal infection; requires appropriate patient selection |

items.title: Reading list and linked references
items.body:
## Primary guidelines, curriculum and exam reports

- **1.** **ANZCA.** Anaesthesia Training Program Curriculum, version 1.14, December 2025. User-supplied document; the primary source for outcome terminology and codes.
- **2.** **SCCM/European Society of Intensive Care Medicine.** [Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock (2026)](https://www.sccm.org/clinical-resources/guidelines/guidelines/surviving-sepsis-campaign-international-guidelines-for-management-of-sepsis-and-septic-shock-2026). Central evidence source for antibiotic and source-control timing, fluids, vasopressors, steroids and organ support.
- **3.** **ANZCA.** [PG28 Infection Prevention and Control (2025)](https://www.anzca.edu.au/getContentAsset/41b75be4-4c78-4318-8ac4-3d0dd2ca8f8f/80feb437-d24d-46b8-a858-4a2a28b9b970/PG28-Infection-prevention-and-control-2025.pdf?language=en). Equipment reprocessing, injection safety, airway devices, infection precautions and theatre practice.
- **4.** **ANZAAG/ANZCA.** [Perioperative Anaphylaxis Management Guideline (2022)](https://www.anzca.edu.au/resources/professional-documents/endorsed-guidelines/anaphylaxis-guideline-2022.pdf). Australian/New Zealand adult and paediatric crisis algorithms, adrenaline, fluids and post-crisis response; consult the [ANZCA algorithm/card collection](https://www.anzca.edu.au/safety-and-advocacy/standards-of-practice/perioperative-anaphylaxis-management-guidelines) in practice.
- **5.** **ANZCA.** [PG69 Prevention, Investigation and Follow-up of Perioperative Hypersensitivity Reactions and Anaphylaxis (2025)](https://www.anzca.edu.au/getContentAsset/0f526e72-c35f-46d7-a816-746e63f92079/80feb437-d24d-46b8-a858-4a2a28b9b970/PG69-Perioperative-hypersensitivity-reactions-2025.pdf?language=en). Specialist referral, testing, documentation, future anaesthetic planning.
- **6.** **IDSA.** [Guidance on Treatment of Antimicrobial-Resistant Gram-Negative Infections (2026 update)](https://www.idsociety.org/practice-guideline/amr-guidance/). Resistance mechanism and ESBL/AmpC/CRE/DTR-Pseudomonas treatment interpretation; supersedes the 2024 version.
- **7.** **ASHP/IDSA/SIS/SHEA.** [Clinical Practice Guidelines for Antimicrobial Prophylaxis in Surgery](https://academic.oup.com/ajhp/article/70/3/195/5112717). Procedure-dependent prophylaxis, administration timing and cefazolin redosing; reconcile with current local surgical guidance.
- **8.** **ANZCA Final Examination Chairs’ Reports (provided):** 2023.2, 2024.2, 2025.1, 2025.2 and 2026.1; read question-specific examiner standards alongside curriculum, not as evidence for obsolete recommendations.

## BJA Education and complementary clinical reading

- **1.** **Dewachter P, Savic L.** [Perioperative anaphylaxis: pathophysiology, clinical presentation and management](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7807982/). BJA Education 2019;19:313–320. Useful for mediator physiology, absent cutaneous signs, testing and differential; use ANZAAG for local doses.
- **2.** Manigrasso J, Desai N, Naoum E. Maternal sepsis: background, diagnosis and management. BJA Education 2024;24:389–398. DOI 10.1016/j.bjae.2024.06.004. Maternal sepsis assessment and treatment; cite alongside obstetric guidelines.
- **3.** **BJA Education.** [Metabolic acidosis in anaesthesia and critical care](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10874758/). Relevant to lactate interpretation, acid–base differential and selected bicarbonate decisions.
- **4.** **Sepsis-3 task force (Singer et al).** [Third International Consensus Definitions for Sepsis and Septic Shock](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2492881). JAMA 2016. Definitions, SOFA and septic shock phenotype; SIRS terminology retained in curriculum for historical comparison.
- **5.** **NAP6 investigators.** [Anaesthesia, surgery and life-threatening allergic reactions: sixth National Audit Project](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29935567/). Epidemiology, suspected triggers and serious perioperative outcomes; local incidence may vary.

## ANZCA Blue Book chapters audited (relevant editions)

- Chang K, Haseeb A, Khoyratty S. The emergency laparotomy patient. Australasian Anaesthesia 2025, pp 131–148. Source control, NELA/SORT, frailty, perioperative emergency-laparotomy care.  [https://hdl.handle.net/11055/1386](https://hdl.handle.net/11055/1386)
- Martyr L, Cook S, Senthuran S. Keep calm and know sepsis. Australasian Anaesthesia 2019. Useful for sepsis physiology and history; apply current 2026 SSC recommendations instead of historical algorithms.  [https://www.anzca.edu.au/getContentAsset/23f2add6-d29f-495a-a094-81157ded47b3/80feb437-d24d-46b8-a858-4a2a28b9b970/Blue-Book-2019.pdf?language=en](https://www.anzca.edu.au/getContentAsset/23f2add6-d29f-495a-a094-81157ded47b3/80feb437-d24d-46b8-a858-4a2a28b9b970/Blue-Book-2019.pdf?language=en)
- Nguyen TM, Szental J, Bramley D. A narrative review of the perioperative management of DMARDs. Australasian Anaesthesia 2023, pp 23–36. Balance infection and flare risks with medication holds.  [https://hdl.handle.net/11055/1194](https://hdl.handle.net/11055/1194)
- Platt PR, Sadleir P, Clarke R. Anaphylactic shock under anaesthesia: a reappraisal of the pathophysiology and management. Australasian Anaesthesia 2015. Historic pathophysiology; current ANZAAG takes priority.  [https://www.anzca.edu.au/getContentAsset/5d46b97a-87c1-4055-8ebf-cac65388433a/80feb437-d24d-46b8-a858-4a2a28b9b970/Blue-Book-2015.pdf?language=en](https://www.anzca.edu.au/getContentAsset/5d46b97a-87c1-4055-8ebf-cac65388433a/80feb437-d24d-46b8-a858-4a2a28b9b970/Blue-Book-2015.pdf?language=en)

- Pisano A, Venditto M, Palmieri C, Landoni G. Novel therapies and interventions in sepsis and septic shock. BJA Education 2025;25:206–217.  [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bjae.2025.01.003](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bjae.2025.01.003)

## Evidence audit and boundaries

**Examiner report application check.** The supplied **2026.1** report tested management under the 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign, physiological optimisation for emergency surgery in severe sepsis, and decision-making for transfer of a deteriorating septic patient. The **2025.2** report listed steroid treatment in septic shock and paediatric anaphylaxis. The **2025.1** report identified major omissions in severe maternal pneumonia answers when candidates described fetal management but not maternal ventilation, circulation and antibiotics. The **2024.2** report examined grade 2 anaphylaxis during emergency surgery and obstructive urosepsis; the **2023.2** report examined septic shock recommendations and perioperative anaphylaxis. These scenarios informed the practical clinical reasoning woven into Chapters 2, 3 and 6; historical examiner questions are not evidence that an older guideline remains correct.

Evidence-audit boundaries. The supplied workbook has now been checked row by row, and all 20 rows have identifiable teaching sections (15 complete-assigned outcomes and five allocated components). Publicly accessible Blue Book editions (2015, 2019, 2023 and 2025) were checked for relevant chapters. The 2019 sepsis and 2015 anaphylaxis chapters inform mechanisms and historical perspectives but are not used to override the 2026 SSC, 2025 PG69, or current ANZAAG crisis guidance. Proprietary textbook and subscription-only full-text access was not independently verified; evidence certainty remains variable for local antimicrobial doses, neuraxial placement during infection, rescue anaphylaxis therapies and individualised surgery timing. Clinicians must cross-check current local NZ prescribing, emergency pathways and infection-prevention policies. The mapping audit is complete for the provided workbook sheet, not for all ANZCA learning outcomes assigned to other sets.
